15756.rationale: Free (detached, re-anastomosed) muscle flap is not Transfer: Replacement of recipient soft tissue with autologous tissue plus Excision of donor muscle (B3.9).
15756.note: Merged B's donor/recipient sets with A's ulcer alternative, given a specified site (L97.81-). A chronic ulcer moves the case from 500-502 to MDC 9 579-581; a diabetic ulcer (E11.62x) would be principal and group elsewhere.

pcs_sets.note: thigh skin flap to right lower leg
thigh skin flap to left lower leg
forearm skin flap to right lower leg

15757.rationale: Free fasciocutaneous flap = Replacement of recipient subcutaneous tissue with autologous tissue plus Excision of donor subcutaneous tissue (B3.9).
15757.note: Merged B's sets with A's ulcer alternative, given a specified site (L97.81-). The ulcer moves the case from 463-465 to 570-572 because the donor subcutaneous Excision is a debridement code in MDC 9.

15758.rationale: Free fascial flap = Replacement of recipient subcutaneous tissue/fascia with autologous tissue plus Excision of donor fascia (B3.9).
15758.note: Merged B's foot/hand recipients and foot osteomyelitis with A's ulcer alternative, here a foot ulcer (L97.51-). It moves the case from 463-465 to 570-572.

20957.rationale: Free vascularized metatarsal to replace lost hand bone = Replacement of metacarpal with autologous tissue plus Excision of metatarsal donor (B3.9).
20957.note: Took B: free metatarsal transfer is a hand/metacarpal reconstruction far more often than a jaw one; A's mandible recipient was the outlier. Rare in Medicare either way.

pcs_sets.note: right mandible defect, right scapula donor
left mandible defect, left scapula donor

20962.rationale: Vascularized bone takes the place of a resected jaw segment = Replacement with autologous tissue, open; bone harvest from a separate site coded as Excision per B3.9; scapula used as the representative non-fibula, non-iliac donor.
20962.note: Took B: same mandible sets as A plus a maxilla recipient (scapula is a common maxillary donor, groups 143-145); dropped A's radius set since a radial osteocutaneous flap belongs to the osteocutaneous code.

pcs_sets.note: right mandible defect, fibula osteocutaneous donor
left mandible defect, fibula osteocutaneous donor

20969.rationale: Osteocutaneous free flap rebuilding a jaw segment = Replacement of mandible/maxilla with autologous tissue, open, plus Excision of the donor bone (B3.9); fibula is the usual donor in this code's range; skin paddle not coded separately.
20969.note: Merged: B's fibula sets including the maxilla recipient (143-145) plus A's scapula osteocutaneous donor set.

pcs_sets.note: right mandible defect, right iliac crest donor
left mandible defect, left iliac crest donor

20970.rationale: Iliac crest osteocutaneous free flap to a jaw defect = Replacement of mandible/maxilla with autologous tissue, open, plus Excision of pelvic bone at the donor site (B3.9).
20970.note: Took B: same mandible sets as A plus an iliac-crest-to-maxilla recipient set, which groups 143-145.

21268.rationale: Orbital box osteotomy with repositioning = Reposition orbit with internal fixation, bone graft Supplement, calvarial donor Excision; the craniotomy is access.
21268.note: Same PCS in both passes; took B's dx: the index sends congenital orbital deformity to Q10.7 (A's Q75.8 is a nonspecific skull/face code that shifts to MDC 8). Acquired causes (H05.32-/H05.33-) also group 113-114, so no alternative.

21602.rationale: Chest wall tumor removal with rib segments = Excision of ribs; reconstruction coded separately as Supplement chest wall with synthetic substitute.
21602.note: Took A: mesh reconstruction is the reconstruction within this code; B's latissimus flap set dropped because a muscle flap is a separately reported operation.

pcs_sets.note: 3 or more ribs, mesh, mediastinal nodes

21603.rationale: As the version without nodes, plus mediastinal node dissection coded separately (B3.10c) as Excision of thorax lymphatic.
21603.note: Took A: as 21602, B's separately reported flap set dropped; node dissection kept as Excision of thorax lymphatic (station dissection, not a whole chain); same family either way.

pcs_sets.note: brachial plexus release via first or cervical rib removal

21615.rationale: Rib removal frees the brachial plexus, so Release of brachial plexus, open (B3.13); the rib is the restraining tissue, not coded separately.
21615.note: Took B's plexus Release (Coding Clinic 2Q 2016 treats rib removal in TOS decompression as the means of releasing the plexus); dropped B's venous-TOS sets and I82B11, rare in Medicare and paired with G540 they mis-group.

21616.rationale: Rib removal frees the brachial plexus (Release, B3.13) and a segment of the upper thoracic sympathetic chain is cut out as a separate objective (Excision).
21616.note: Took B: plexus Release per the TOS Coding Clinic, plus sympathectomy coded separately as Excision of thoracic sympathetic nerve (separate objective, Coding Clinic 2Q 2017).

21620.rationale: Part of the sternum is cut out = Excision, sternum, open; usual Medicare indication is post-cardiac-surgery sternal infection.
21620.note: Took B: post-sternotomy infection sequences first as the complication code (T81.4-), osteomyelitis as additional; sternal metastasis kept as the family-changing alternative.

pcs_sets.note: scalene division with cervical rib removal

21705.rationale: Cutting the scalene and removing the cervical rib both free the brachial plexus = Release, brachial plexus (B3.13); alternative view is Division of neck muscle plus Excision of rib.
21705.note: Took B: scalene division and cervical rib removal both serve to free the plexus, so one Release code (B3.13) rather than A's Division of muscle plus rib Excision.

22318.rationale: Anterior odontoid screw = Reposition of cervical vertebra with internal fixation (Insertion if nondisplaced, per B3.15).
22318.note: Took A: B3.15 makes screw fixation of a nondisplaced dens fracture Insertion (515-517) and reduction of a displaced one Reposition (518-520); B dropped the nondisplaced variant.

22610.rationale: Single-level posterolateral thoracic fusion = Fusion of thoracic vertebral joint, posterior approach posterior column, autologous graft, open.
22610.note: Took B: same fusion code as A; kept B's spinal-metastasis alternative because metastatic disease is a common reason for thoracic posterior fusion in Medicare and moves the case to 456-458.

pcs_sets.note: thoracolumbar to lumbar span, interbody devices (typical adult)
thoracic span ending at T12-L1 (less common in Medicare)

22812.rationale: Anterior deformity fusion over 8+ vertebrae: one Fusion code per joint region spanned, anterior approach anterior column; adult degenerative curves usually cross into the lumbar spine.
22812.note: Merged: B's dx (adult deformity coded M41.8-) and B's thoracic-only sets, with A's all-interbody thoracolumbar-lumbar span as typical; family follows the span coded (523-525 vs 456-458).

pcs_sets.note: right thumb from right great toe, iliac bone graft
left thumb from left great toe, iliac bone graft
right thumb from left great toe, iliac bone graft

26551.rationale: Microvascular toe tissue to rebuild thumb = Replacement of thumb with toe (qualifier names donor toe); separately harvested iliac bone graft = Excision of pelvic bone per B3.9.
26551.note: Took B: delayed reconstruction for an acquired thumb loss is the norm. A's acute traumatic-amputation alternative (906) is uncommon for toe-to-hand transfer, so it is dropped.

26553.rationale: Single lesser toe free transfer: to thumb = Replacement of thumb with toe; to finger there is no toe-qualified finger code, so Replacement of finger phalanx with autologous tissue plus Detachment of donor toe (B3.9).
26553.note: Took B: thumb recipients (toe qualifier) plus finger recipients (Replacement of the finger phalanx plus toe Detachment, B3.9); all sets group 939-941. A's acute-amputation alternative is dropped as uncommon.

27132.rationale: Total hip = Replacement of hip joint (ceramic-on-poly uncemented as the common construct); removal of prior femoral fixation is a distinct body part, Removal from upper femur.
27132.note: Took B: hardware removal from the upper femur is a separate body part (B3.2) and groups 498-499 (v44 App. D ranks it above 469-470). The no-hardware variant (retained or previously removed hardware) is kept because it groups 469-470.

27185.rationale: Growth-plate arrest of the trochanteric apophysis indexes to Repair (no device) or Insertion of internal fixation (screws/staples), upper femur, open.
27185.note: Took A: the PCS index sends epiphysiodesis to Repair (drilling/curettage) or Insertion (screws/staples), not Destruction. Every set groups 480-482.

27280.rationale: Open SI joint fusion with graft and hardware = Fusion sacroiliac joint, autologous tissue device (B3.10c applied by analogy; 0SG704Z is the alternative and groups the same); bilateral = two codes.
27280.note: Merged B's device value with A's bilateral set. Not a grouper error: v44 lists both SI fusion codes in the single-level posterior list of DRGs 447-448 ('two or more codes'), so bilateral SI fusion really is 447-448. Unilateral is 450-451.

27295.rationale: Hip disarticulation = Detachment at femoral region (the lower-limb analog of shoulder-region disarticulation); 0Y6C0Z1 (upper leg, high) is the competing choice.
27295.note: Took A: Detachment at the femoral region as both passes coded it. A keeps the osteomyelitis alternative because infection is a common reason for hip disarticulation and moves the case from 239-241 to 474-476.

27365.rationale: Radical bone tumor removal: Resection when the whole distal femur body part goes, else Excision; reconstruction reported separately.
27365.note: Took A: a wide resection that takes the whole distal femur is Resection of lower femur (480-482); a partial or intercalary one is Excision (498-499). B dropped the Resection reading, so both are kept here.

27580.rationale: Knee arthrodesis = Fusion knee joint with fixation device, open; typical Medicare case is salvage of failed infected arthroplasty.
27580.note: Took A: fusion with an internal or external device, plus restoring the spacer-removal variant (separate Removal objective, B3.2), which is common in staged salvage after infected TKA. In v44, spacer removal leads to 463-465.

31805.rationale: Suture of an intrathoracic tracheal tear = Repair trachea, open; iatrogenic intubation tears carry a complication dx.
31805.note: Took B: intrathoracic tracheal tears in Medicare patients are often iatrogenic (intubation, esophagectomy), so the J95.7x alternative is common and moves the case to 907-909.

32160.rationale: Open-chest cardiac massage is indexed in PCS to Repair heart, open; principal dx in practice is the cause of the arrest.
32160.note: Took B: the PCS Index sends open-chest cardiac massage to Repair heart, open (02QA0ZZ); A's 5A12012 is the external-massage entry.

32653.rationale: Clearing fibrin, clot or foreign body from the pleural space = Extirpation of matter from pleural cavity, thoracoscopic; non-OR in MS-DRG terms, groups by diagnosis (empyema vs retained hemothorax).
32653.note: Merged: same PCS in both; A's empyema as typical (more common in Medicare) plus B's retained traumatic hemothorax as the family-changing alternative.

32664.rationale: Thoracoscopic interruption of the thoracic sympathetic chain: excised segment = Excision, cautery ablation = Destruction, percutaneous endoscopic; Medicare inpatients are mostly cardiac denervation for refractory VT.
32664.note: Took B: Medicare inpatients having this are mostly cardiac sympathetic denervation for refractory VT; hyperhidrosis (A's typical) kept as alternative; Destruction set kept for ablation technique.

32673.rationale: Thoracoscopic thymectomy = Resection of thymus, percutaneous endoscopic; thymoma NOS indexes to D15.0, malignant/invasive thymoma or thymic carcinoma to C37.
32673.note: Merged: PCS agreed; ICD-10-CM Index defaults thymoma to D15.0 (B), and C37 (A) applies when documented malignant; that split replaces myasthenia gravis, an uncommon thymectomy indication over 65.

32905.rationale: Multiple ribs taken out so the chest wall collapses into the cavity = Excision, 3+ ribs; Schede variant also excises parietal pleura.
32905.note: Took B: the code spans extrapleural and Schede thoracoplasty; Schede also excises parietal pleura (distinct body part, B3.2), which A omitted and which moves the family.

38380.rationale: Tying or oversewing the duct closes its lumen = Occlusion of thoracic duct, open; the neck approach is mainly for chyle leak after neck dissection (I97.89), which groups as an unrelated OR procedure.
38380.note: Merged: B's dx (cervical approach is mainly for post-neck-dissection chyle leak, chylothorax as alternative); dropped B's Repair set since suturing a leaking duct closes the lumen = Occlusion.

38564.rationale: Limited retroperitoneal staging sampling = Excision of aortic lymphatic, open, diagnostic qualifier; without X it groups 987-989.
38564.note: Took A: para-aortic staging sampling is mainly a gynecologic-oncology (endometrial) operation; kidney cancer is not a common principal dx for it. Both passes kept X and Z sets.

38765.rationale: Groin dissection in continuity with iliac/obturator nodes = Resection of inguinal and pelvis lymphatics, open (B3.10b); Excision of inguinal if only part of the chain is taken.
38765.note: Took A: this CPT is groin dissection in continuity with external iliac/hypogastric/obturator nodes, so pelvis lymphatic Resection must be reported with inguinal; B coded inguinal only.

39000.rationale: Cervical mediastinotomy: code the objective achieved, usually Drainage of mediastinum, open; Inspection if exploration only; diagnostic Excision if biopsy.
39000.note: Took A: the CPT spans drainage, exploration and biopsy; B dropped the Inspection set, which groups to a different family (163-165) and is a real variant.

39010.rationale: Transthoracic/sternotomy mediastinotomy: Drainage of mediastinum, open, for the usual infected case; Inspection or diagnostic Excision for other objectives.
39010.note: Took A: adds the biopsy set and the post-sternotomy organ/space SSI alternative (T81.43XA, 856-858), common for sternotomy-approach mediastinal drainage in Medicare.

39560.rationale: Removing part of the diaphragm = Excision, diaphragm, open; primary closure not coded.
39560.note: Took A: same PCS in both; mesothelioma is a likelier Medicare indication for diaphragm excision than primary diaphragm sarcoma (B), and secondary diaphragm cancer kept as the family-changing alternative.

43400.rationale: Open suture ligation of varices = Occlusion of esophageal vein, open; I85.1- carries a code-first note so cirrhosis is sequenced first.
43400.note: Took B: I85.1- carries a code-first note, so cirrhosis is principal (423-425); A sequenced the secondary varices first. Kept I85.01 alternative for undocumented cause (326-328).

43460.rationale: Blind-placed balloon tube to stop variceal bleeding = Control bleeding in GI tract via natural opening; pressure hemostasis fits Control (B3.7); grouper treats this code as OR, so with cirrhosis principal it lands in 981-983.
43460.note: Took B: both chose Control of GI tract bleeding (B3.7, correct); B sequences cirrhosis first per the I85.1- code-first note (981-983), with I85.01 alternative (347-349). Insertion of an esophageal intraluminal device is the weaker reading and was not added.

43771.rationale: Repositioning/adjusting the existing band = Revision, extraluminal device, stomach, percutaneous endoscopic.
43771.note: Took A: band revision is done for a band complication (slip, erosion), so K95.09 typical; revision for poor weight loss is usually a band replacement or conversion, so B's obesity alternative isn't common for this code.

43832.rationale: Constructing a gastric-wall tube brought to the skin = Bypass stomach to cutaneous, open.
43832.note: Took B: open gastrostomy is non-OR in v44 so dx decides; a permanent gastric tube is usually for neurologic dysphagia, and when the cause is a prior stroke I69.391 is sequenced over the symptom code. Kept R13.10 as the alternative.

43848.rationale: No device-free Revision root op; code what is done: redo of the bypass, excision to resize the pouch, (band/ring removal alone would be Removal of extraluminal device).
43848.note: Merged: B's record (keeps the common weight-regain alternative E66.01, 619-621) plus A's ring-removal set, which B dropped because of how it grouped (981-983 with obesity dx).

43881.rationale: Placing gastric stimulator electrodes in the antral wall = Insertion of stimulator lead into stomach, open.
43881.note: Took B: K31.84 has a code-first note, so diabetic gastroparesis puts E11.43 first (040-042); idiopathic K31.84 kept as alternative (981-983, since v44 lists 0DH60MZ in no MDC 6 DRG).

43882.rationale: Repositioning/repairing the lead = Revision of stimulator lead in stomach; taking it out = Removal; open.
43882.note: Merged: B's sets and device-complication dx (907-909) plus A's K31.84 alternative for removal or revision when therapy fails (981-983 removal, 326-328 revision).

44025.rationale: Open colotomy: Extirpation of the colon segment for an object, diagnostic Excision for biopsy, Inspection of lower tract when only explored.
44025.note: Took B: specific colon segments instead of A's nonspecific large-intestine body part, and keeps the exploration-only variant, which is correctly Inspection and groups 356-358 rather than 344-346.

44050.rationale: Open detorsion/reduction returns bowel to its normal position = Reposition of the affected intestine.
44050.note: Took B: same root operation as A but the specific segment rather than A's whole large intestine; the sigmoid variant groups 344-346, so it stays as its own set.

44055.rationale: Ladd procedure = Release duodenum + Release mesentery + Resection appendix (distinct body parts); add Reposition of small intestine when a volvulus is untwisted.
44055.note: Took B: adds the mesenteric Release and the volvulus-reduction variant the CPT explicitly covers (329-331); A had only the band-division reading.

44187.rationale: Laparoscopic stoma creation = Bypass ileum (or jejunum) to cutaneous, percutaneous endoscopic.
44187.note: Took B: same PCS; dropped A's pressure-ulcer alternative because fecal diversion for sacral wounds is done by colostomy (kept on 44320), not ileostomy, so it is not a common dx here.

pcs_sets.note: Hartmann reversal, stomal descending colon excised

44227.rationale: Laparoscopic stoma takedown with resection: the stoma-bearing bowel is removed and rejoined = Excision of that segment; anastomosis and mobilization are integral.
44227.note: New for the colostomy set: Excision per Coding Clinic convention (takedown with any bowel removed = Excision, anastomosis inherent); rejected A's Reposition (bowel is removed, not just moved) and B's Bypass (reversal restores the native route, it does not reroute). Kept both passes' ileum Excision; Z43.3 typical as lap Hartmann reversal dominates this code (same family as Z43.2).

44320.rationale: Open colostomy/cecostomy = Bypass of the colon segment to cutaneous; diversion for a stage 4 sacral ulcer is a common Medicare indication that groups to 981-983.
44320.note: Took B: same PCS as A plus the pressure-ulcer diversion alternative, which is common for this code and changes the family (981-983).

pcs_sets.note: stoma relocated to a new site

44345.rationale: In-depth colostomy revision: Excision when stenotic/prolapsed stomal colon is cut out (usual), Repair when only refashioned, Reposition when the stoma is moved to a new site.
44345.note: Merged: A's Excision and Reposition (relocation groups 344-346, so kept as its own set) with B's Repair reading; Excision listed first as the usual in-depth revision, consistent with the takedown convention.

pcs_sets.note: reading: colon revision integral, abdominal wall only

44346.rationale: Parastomal hernia repair (Supplement with mesh or Repair of abdominal wall) plus the colostomy revision on a distinct body part per B3.2a (Repair, Excision, or Reposition if relocated).
44346.note: Merged: B's structure (the CPT includes colostomy revision, a separate body part, so the colon is coded; 329-331) plus A's mesh-with-Excision set; kept A's abdominal-wall-only reading last because some coders treat the stoma refashioning as integral (353-355).

44620.rationale: Stoma closure without bowel removed: the objective is closing the opening in the stoma-bearing bowel = Repair; Reposition is the competing reading.
44620.note: Took B (Repair): no segment removed so Excision does not apply, there is no rerouting, and freeing the loop from the wall is a step to the closure; kept A's Reposition as a transverse-colon set because it groups 344-346 (for ileum both readings give 329-331).

pcs_sets.note: stomal descending colon excised, joined to rectal stump
stomal sigmoid excised, joined to rectal stump

44626.rationale: Hartmann reversal: the stoma-bearing colon end is resected and anastomosed to the rectal stump = Excision of that colon; anastomosis and mobilization integral.
44626.note: New: this CPT includes resection, and Coding Clinic convention codes a takedown with bowel removed as Excision with the anastomosis inherent; rejected A's Reposition (minor bowel 344-346; bowel is removed, not just moved) and B's Bypass (reversal restores, not reroutes). Lands 329-331.

45130.rationale: Perineal rectosigmoidectomy: full-thickness bowel cut and peritoneum entered through the perineum = open approach; a distal rectal cuff stays, so Excision rectum (plus sigmoid when taken).
45130.note: Took B: A's Resection is wrong since a distal cuff remains (B3.8), and approach 7 is for transanal local excision (0DBP7ZZ would fall to 347-349); sigmoid-inclusive set kept since it moves 332-334 to 329-331.

48153.rationale: Pancreatic head Excision, duodenum Excision (proximal cuff kept), gallbladder Resection, distal CBD Excision, all open; no gastric code since the stomach/pylorus is kept.
48153.note: Took B: pylorus-preserving resection leaves a proximal duodenal cuff, so it is Excision of the duodenum, not Resection. The duodenal-cancer alternative therefore groups to 326-328, not 329-331.

48154.rationale: Pancreatic head Excision, duodenum Excision (proximal cuff kept), gallbladder Resection, distal CBD Excision, all open.
48154.note: Took B: pylorus-preserving resection leaves a proximal duodenal cuff, so it is Excision of the duodenum, not Resection. The duodenal-cancer alternative therefore groups to 326-328, not 329-331.

49062.rationale: Internal drainage of a lymphocele into the peritoneum = Drainage of the cavity holding it (pelvic cavity or retroperitoneum), open.
49062.note: Took B: a lymphocele is a collection in a body cavity, not a lymphatic vessel, so Drainage of pelvic cavity/retroperitoneum beats A's pelvic-lymphatic Drainage; B's postprocedural vs transplant-complication dx split is real.

49188.rationale: Same as smaller size bands: Excision of the containing body part or Destruction; size does not change PCS.
49188.note: Took A: at 10-20 cm summed diameter both peritoneal-metastasis debulking and retroperitoneal sarcoma are common, so keep C78.6 typical with C48.0 as the family-changing alternative B dropped.

49189.rationale: Large non-organ tumor, most often retroperitoneal sarcoma: Excision, retroperitoneum (or mesentery/peritoneum/omentum), open.
49189.note: Took A: retroperitoneal sarcoma typical, but extensive carcinomatosis debulking also reaches this size band, so keep A's C78.6 alternative (different family).

49190.rationale: Very large non-organ tumor, most often retroperitoneal liposarcoma: Excision, retroperitoneum (or mesentery/peritoneum/omentum), open.
49190.note: Took A: same reasoning as 49189; C78.6 alternative restored because large-volume peritoneal debulking is a common use.

49215.rationale: Presacral space is extraperitoneal: Excision, retroperitoneum, open; add Resection of coccyx when the coccyx is taken en bloc.
49215.note: Took B: the Neoplasm Table sends presacral-region benign tumors to D36.7, not D20.0 (retroperitoneum); PCS sets identical in both passes.

49255.rationale: Omentectomy = Excision of omentum when partial (usual infracolic), Resection when the whole omentum is removed.
49255.note: Took A: standalone omentectomy for omental disease takes C78.6 even with an ovarian primary (treatment directed at the metastasis), so B's C56.9 alternative is not a common principal dx here.

pcs_sets.note: right, Release of kidney pelvis (B3.13 reading)
left, Release of kidney pelvis (B3.13 reading)
right, vessel moved off UPJ coded as Reposition of renal artery
left, vessel moved off UPJ coded as Reposition of renal artery
right, vessel divided coded as Occlusion of renal artery
left, vessel divided coded as Occlusion of renal artery

50100.rationale: Freeing the UPJ from a crossing vessel = Release of kidney pelvis (B3.13 codes the body part freed); coders may instead code the vessel work as Reposition or Occlusion of renal artery; open.
50100.note: Merged: B's Release reading as typical plus A's Reposition and Occlusion readings; Occlusion moves the family to 673-675, so the real ambiguity is kept visible.

50205.rationale: Open kidney biopsy = Excision, kidney, open, diagnostic qualifier; done for medical renal disease when a needle biopsy is unsafe.
50205.note: Took B: a renal mass is rarely biopsied open (needle biopsy or partial nephrectomy instead), so A's mass alternative is not common enough to keep.

pcs_sets.note: right, no cuff or cuff taken transurethrally
left, no cuff or cuff taken transurethrally

50548.rationale: Laparoscopic nephroureterectomy = Resection kidney + Resection ureter, perc endoscopic; a bladder cuff is a distinct body part coded as Excision of bladder.
50548.note: Took B, cuff sets first: the cuff is standard for upper-tract cancer and moves the case to 653-655, but a transurethral cuff (0TBB8ZZ) or none stays 656-658, so both families are real.

50600.rationale: Open ureterotomy = Drainage of ureter (device value when a tube stays in the ureter, which is non-OR and groups medical); exploration alone = Inspection of ureter.
50600.note: Merged: A's no-device Drainage sets (659-661) plus B's device and Inspection variants; kept A's specific N131 over B's unspecified N139.

50605.rationale: Stent placed through an open ureterotomy to hold an obstructed ureter open = Dilation, ureter, intraluminal device, open; non-OR in MS-DRG terms, groups by diagnosis.
50605.note: Took A: stented strictures usually have hydronephrosis (N131, 693-694); N135 is the no-hydronephrosis code and CMS's own v44 Appendix B lists it under 689-690, so that family is CMS's, not a grouper error.

pcs_sets.note: ileal conduit stoma, mesh hernia repair

50728.rationale: Stoma revision = Repair of the conduit body part (ileum or ureter) plus the abdominal wall: Repair for a fascial closure, Supplement when mesh is placed.
50728.note: Merged A and B: A's mesh variant (groups 981-983, since mesh Supplement has no MDC 11 row) is a common real case and kept; B's ureterostomy stomas added.

50815.rationale: Colon conduit = Bypass ureter(s) to colocutaneous plus Excision of the colon segment taken for it (B3.9).
50815.note: Merged: A's laterality sets + B's transverse colon set; benign dx typical (conduit without cystectomy), bladder cancer kept as alternative for palliative diversion (656-658).

50820.rationale: Ileal conduit = Bypass ureter(s) to ileocutaneous plus Excision of the harvested ileal segment (B3.9).
50820.note: Merged: identical PCS sets; A's benign dx as typical since with cancer the conduit is usually billed with the cystectomy code, B's bladder cancer kept as alternative (656-658).

pcs_sets.note: right colon pouch with ileal limb

50825.rationale: Continent cutaneous reservoir = Bypass ureters to colocutaneous or ileocutaneous plus Excision of each bowel segment harvested to build it.
50825.note: Took A: a continent pouch without cystectomy is built for benign disease; cancer patients get it with cystectomy (a different code), so the cancer alternative is not common here.

50860.rationale: Ureter brought to the skin = Bypass ureter to cutaneous, open.
50860.note: Took B: standalone cutaneous ureterostomy in older adults is mostly palliative diversion for pelvic cancer; benign obstruction kept as the alternative (659-661).

50930.rationale: Fistula closed on both sides: Repair ureter plus Repair of the involved bowel segment (separate body systems).
50930.note: Took B, restoring the bowel variant A dropped for grouping: this code is for ureter-bowel fistulas; ureterovaginal fistulas are usually fixed by reimplantation, which is a different code.

51800.rationale: Bladder neck plasty = Repair (PCS index: cystoplasty to Repair); widening by incision and flap can also read as Dilation, which is non-OR; fundus reduction = Excision of bladder.
51800.note: Merged: A's Repair (653-655) as the index-supported reading, B's Dilation (medical 698-700) kept as the defensible other reading, and B's fundus Excision; dropped wedge resection alone, an add-on.

54390.rationale: Epispadias correction in an exstrophy patient: reconstruct the dorsal urethra (Repair urethra) and correct the penile deformity (Repair penis), open; Supplement if graft/flap tissue is used.
54390.note: Took B: the CPT is the epispadias (urethral/penile) repair in an exstrophy patient; bladder closure is a separate CPT, so A's bladder Repair over-codes it. Penis procedures 709-710 with epispadias as principal.

55650.rationale: Removal of the whole seminal vesicle = Resection of seminal vesicle, open, by laterality.
55650.note: Took B: the same Resection codes. It keeps a benign cyst alternative because primary seminal vesicle cancer is rare, benign cystic disease is at least as common, and the cyst moves the case to 717-718.

58240.rationale: Each organ removed = Resection; ileal conduit = Bypass ureters to ileocutaneous plus ileum Excision; end colostomy = Bypass sigmoid to cutaneous.
58240.note: Took B: adds urethra resection (removed with the bladder in female anterior exenteration) and the post-hysterectomy total exenteration variant (recurrent endometrial cancer), which groups to 748 under v44.

58520.rationale: Suture repair of nonobstetric uterine rupture = Repair, uterus, open.
58520.note: Took A: iatrogenic perforation (N9971) is the plausible Medicare cause of nonobstetric uterine rupture needing repair; traumatic laceration (B) is rare at this age; confidence lowered to low.

58700.rationale: Whole tube removed = Resection of fallopian tube, open; part of one tube = Excision; Medicare indication is chronic tubal disease.
58700.note: Merged: B's sets plus a left partial set; dropped B's ectopic alternative (not a Medicare population) and A's bilateral partial set (that is sterilization, not a Medicare indication).

58822.rationale: This code is the abdominal (open) approach, despite CMS's short descriptor; Drainage of ovary, open, drain device if left in; surgical, not bedside.
58822.note: Merged: B's open-approach sets (the code is the abdominal approach; A followed CMS's percutaneous short descriptor) with A's tubo-ovarian abscess diagnosis.

58940.rationale: Open oophorectomy = Resection of ovary (total) or Excision (partial), by side; malignant pathology moves the case to the malignancy family.
58940.note: Merged: B's sets and cancer alternative (common for a postmenopausal adnexal mass; 731-733 vs 742-743), with A's side-neutral D279 since the sets span both sides.

pcs_sets.note: complete pelvic node dissection (Resection), limited aortic (Excision)

58958.rationale: Excision of recurrent peritoneal tumor with omentectomy and node dissection; surgery aimed at the recurrence, not the excised primary, puts the secondary site first; Resection vs Excision of pelvic nodes moves the family only under the ovarian dx.
58958.note: Merged: A's dx (guideline I.C.2.b: treatment directed at the secondary site makes C78.6 principal) with C56.9 kept as alternative; A's Resection-of-pelvic-nodes set plus an Excision set (B's reading), since the full-chain call depends on the op note and splits 734-735 from 749-750.

58960.rationale: Staging/second-look laparotomy: exploration not coded; retroperitoneal node sampling and peritoneal biopsies are diagnostic Excisions; omentectomy as Excision when done.
58960.note: Took B: the CPT describes node sampling, so Excision (not A's Resection of pelvic nodes, which wrongly pushed 734-735); changed node qualifier to diagnostic X since staging samples are biopsies; side-neutral C56.9. Family 749-750 either way.

60522.rationale: Thymus resection plus radical mediastinal dissection coded separately as Resection of thorax lymphatic (B3.10c).
60522.note: Took A: same PCS in both; dropped B's myasthenia alternative because a radical mediastinal dissection implies tumor, and extended thymectomy for myasthenia without thymoma is uncommon in Medicare.

60545.rationale: Adrenal resection plus separate Excision of retroperitoneum for the adjacent tumor.
60545.note: Took A: same PCS in both; adrenal cortex cancer typical (unspecified side, since sets are lateralized) and retroperitoneal sarcoma with adrenal en bloc kept as the common family-changing alternative.

pcs_sets.note: right, internal carotid replaced by graft
left, internal carotid replaced by graft

60605.rationale: Carotid body Resection plus the arterial objective: Excision of the sacrificed external carotid, or Replacement when the internal carotid is resected and grafted.
60605.note: Took B: the external carotid is the artery usually sacrificed (037-039); internal carotid resection needs a graft (Replacement, 040-042); D446 is where the index sends carotid body tumors.
